questions.q: How should this capstone presentation begin, according to the lesson?
options: With the dashboard — thirty seconds on the three pinned tiles before any detailed report page or question
By reading through every DAX measure line by line
With the hidden drillthrough page, before anything else
By explaining the Power Query cleanup steps first
questions.explain: Starting with the dashboard's at-a-glance tiles mirrors how a real stakeholder presentation should open — the headline view first, detail only on request.

questions.q: When should the drillthrough page be used during the presentation?
options: Only if someone specifically asks for territory-level detail — not shown by default
At the very start of every presentation, before the dashboard
It should never be shown under any circumstance
Only if the VP explicitly forbids using slicers
questions.explain: This applies Chapter 8's 'only what the audience needs' principle to a live presentation — detail is available, not forced on every viewer by default.

questions.q: What is the final test for whether this capstone project actually succeeded?
options: Whether someone unfamiliar with the data can name the single most important number on the dashboard in under ten seconds
Whether the report contains at least 20 visuals
Whether every possible DAX function was used somewhere in the model
Whether the semantic model file size exceeds 500 MB
questions.explain: This is the same test Lesson 66 introduced for executive dashboards generally — a finished project succeeds by being immediately clear, not by being feature-dense.

questions.q: How does the lesson recommend checking that the finished project actually meets its original goal?
options: Pull up the written scope from Lesson 84 and confirm every requirement has a specific place in the finished dashboard
Compare the file size to other Power BI files
Count the number of report pages against a fixed target of five
Ask Microsoft support to certify the report
questions.explain: Re-checking against the original written scope (not against a feature checklist) is the correct way to confirm the project does what was actually asked — no more, no less.

questions.q: What does the lesson suggest as a next step after finishing this capstone?
options: Rebuild the same capstone process against a different schema like Northwind or AdventureWorks2012, to practice the same judgment calls elsewhere
Immediately delete the capstone project and start an unrelated one
Never touch Power BI again since the course is complete
Only use this exact same AdventureWorksDW2014 model forever
questions.explain: Practicing the same nine-step process (requirements through security/refresh) against a different, unfamiliar schema reinforces the judgment calls rather than just the specific steps memorized here.
